ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of S$1.80 to the rider for the unexempt 1.28 km deviation on the second loop (fare.distance_fare 33.02 ÷ 23.42 km = S$1.41/km × 1.28 km), noting the driver's breach of the shortest-and-most-direct-route obligation; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat, complaint and driver statement contain no threat, harassment, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation; nothing to escalate. Evidence is sufficient: GPS trace is continuous (30 s thinned samples, no gap > 2 min), chat messages are timestamped, the quoted route and the metered fare are present, and the deviation geometry is readable from the trace.

Segment identification (RydeTAXI, metered — distance tracks mileage, so RD-2's metered branch applies). Quoted route: Hougang Mall → Ang Mo Kio Ave 3 → CTE → AYE → VivoCity, 19.131 km. The trace matches the quoted route from pickup until ~12:51:50, then leaves it: the car goes north to ~1.3646,103.8673 (12:52:50), back south to 1.36365,103.8692 (12:53:50), east to 1.3648,103.8636 (12:54:50) and north to 1.3669,103.8615 (12:55:20), before rejoining the CTE corridor at 1.3622,103.8589 (12:56:20). That is a closed ~2.3 km loop with no net geographic progress — off-route by any reading. A second, similar detour occurs around ~13:07–13:10 near Upper Thomson: 1.3077,103.8421 (13:07:20) → 1.3063,103.8435 → 1.3050,103.8458 (13:08:20) → 1.3057,103.8462 → 1.3031,103.8473 (13:09:20) → 1.3017,103.8496 → 1.3001,103.8521 (13:10:20), ~2.2 km of driving to reach a point (1.2981,103.8546 at 13:10:50) that the quoted route passes essentially directly. After 13:10 the trace again matches the route down the AYE to VivoCity (13:22:10). A single metre-accurate extra_km cannot be computed from thinned samples, so I use the trace geometry: segment 1 (Ang Mo Kio / Serangoon Garden loop) ≈ 2.3 km; segment 2 (Upper Thomson loop) ≈ 1.3 km (≈0.8 km of excess re-driving on top of the ~0.5 km of route it replaces, the CTE/AYE corner at 1.3076,103.8412–1.3050,103.8401). The fare records 23.42 km against the quoted 19.131 km (−0.5 km tolerance ≈ 4.09 km difference), consistent with ≈3.6 km of excess driving.

Segment 1 is exempt: the driver asked before leaving the route (12:46:25) about the jam on Ang Mo Kio Ave 3 and "go round via Serangoon Garden Way", two km before the deviation began (~12:51:50, trace); the rider replied "Sure, go ahead" at 12:47:05. The rider's own complaint concedes this. This is the general-route-consent ground.

Segment 2 counts: the record places it on Upper Thomson Road / Yio Chu Kang, nowhere near Serangoon Garden Way, and the driver's own statement says "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" — i.e. not a riding request. No rider message ties it; there was no second request, and a driver's post-hoc claim (or a GPS reroute) is not consent under RD-5.

Amount (RD-2, metered branch): per-km rate = fare.distance_fare 33.02 ÷ fare.distance_km 23.42 = S$1.41/km. Unexempt excess ≈ 1.28 km × S$1.41 = S$1.80. (With the alternative 0.8 km estimate it would be S$1.13; I take the trace-based 1.28 km.) The metered waiting component (S$0.11/0.85 min) is retained under RD-3(c); unmapped mileage differences inside the 200 m corridor are not refunded. RD-6 does not apply: driver profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this case does not make a "repeated" route violation and no account flag issues.

segment_findings.reason: Driver raised the jam and proposed going round via Serangoon Garden Way at 12:46:25, before the deviation began (~12:51:50); the rider replied 'Sure, go ahead' at 12:47:05 and concedes the point in the complaint. The general route-choice agreement covers the route taken to get past the jam under RD-5, so the ~2.3 km loop at Ang Mo Kio is exempt (RD-3(a)/RD-5).

The agreed route choice was Serangoon Garden Way near the start of the trip; the trace places this second ~1.3 km loop (13:07–13:10) on Upper Thomson Road / Yio Chu Kang, far from that named road, and the driver's own statement attributes it to 'my GPS rerouting'. No rider message before this segment asks for it, and 'whichever route is faster' does not cover a driver's reroute of his own (RD-5), so the excess mileage on this segment is unexempt under RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: A GPS reroute is not rider consent under RD-5; the rider's agreement was to the named Serangoon Garden Way loop near the start and cannot extend to a second loop taken 20 minutes later at Upper Thomson Road. The second segment therefore still counts.
Only the unexempt excess mileage on the second segment is refundable (≈1.28 km × S$1.41/km = S$1.80); the metered fare itself is unaffected, and the first deviation was validly consented to.
